originalTitle: Two rescued after Nairobi building collapse with five still missing
summary: Police have launched a manhunt for the building's owner and contractor after the multi-storey building collapsed while still under construction.
content:
Two people have been pulled alive from the rubble of a building that collapsed in Kenya's capital, Nairobi, on Friday, as a search continues for five still missing.

Police said on Saturday that a manhunt had been launched for the building's owner and the contractor responsible for the site.

Dramatic footage shows the bottom floor of the block, thought to have been 16 or 18 storeys, giving way before the rest of the building crumples, sending a plume of dust into the surrounding streets.

Dozens of builders had been working on the upper floors when it collapsed, but managed to emerge largely unscathed. Those missing were thought to have been in shops at the base of the building.

The incident has raised fresh concerns about construction standards and regulations in Kenya.

The block was under construction when it collapsed on Friday afternoon, with footage showing scaffolding still wrapped around the outside of the building. Officials said 11 shops had already opened on the bottom floors.

Interior ministry official Kipchumba Murkomen said 66 of the 67 construction workers in the building at the time had been able to get out unharmed, while the other had suffered injuries that were not life-threatening.

On Friday, Murkomen said that seven people had been reported missing and rescue teams had made contact with some of those trapped beneath the rubble.

The two survivors rescued on Saturday have been taken to hospital, police said.

Images from the scene, in Nairobi's Eastleigh area, show the concrete floors of the building piled on top of one another, as rescue workers saw through metal to get to those believed to have been stuck underneath.

Footage taken from nearby shows moments before (left) and moments after (right) the building collapsed

Questions have emerged about why the building suddenly collapsed and whether it met planning regulations.

Kenya's National Construction Authority said in a statement that it had identified the company behind the development, as well as the architect and structural engineer, but did not say whether the site had been inspected before Friday.

The National Police Service said it had launched an investigation to establish the cause of the collapse and determine whether anyone was criminally liable.

In a statement it warned that anyone found responsible for negligence or violating building regulations would "face the full force of the law".

Nairobi Governor Sakaja Johnson told local media that the owners of the building did not have the required paperwork for the building to be occupied.

He urged the national government to give local authorities greater powers to penalise "developers who disregard approved building plans and safety standards".

Building collapses are not uncommon in Nairobi, with poor construction or improper planning often cited as contributing factors.

chineseTitle: 内罗毕大楼倒塌后两人获救，五人仍失踪
chineseSummary: 这座仍在建设中的多层建筑倒塌后，警方已对该建筑的业主和承包商展开搜捕。
chineseContent:
周五，肯尼亚首都内罗毕一栋倒塌建筑物的废墟中，有两人被救出，目前仍在继续搜寻仍失踪的五人。

警方周六表示，已对该建筑的业主和负责该工地的承包商展开搜捕。

戏剧性的镜头显示，该街区的底层（据信有 16 或 18 层）在建筑物的其余部分倒塌之前就倒塌了，大量灰尘飞散到周围的街道上。

倒塌时，数十名建筑工人正在楼上施工，但最终毫发无伤。失踪者被认为是在大楼底部的商店里。

该事件引发了人们对肯尼亚建筑标准和法规的新担忧。

周五下午倒塌时，该街区正在施工，视频显示脚手架仍缠绕在建筑物外部。官员称，底层已有 11 家商店开业。

内政部官员Kipchumba Murkomen表示，当时大楼内的67名建筑工人中，有66人毫发无伤，另一人受伤，没有生命危险。

周五，穆尔科曼表示，据报道有七人失踪，救援队已经与一些被困在废墟下的人取得了联系。

警方称，周六获救的两名幸存者已被送往医院。

内罗毕伊斯特利地区的现场图像显示，建筑物的混凝土地板层层叠叠，救援人员正在锯穿金属，以找到​​那些据信被困在下面的人。

从附近拍摄的视频显示了建筑物倒塌之前（左）和之后（右）的瞬间

人们质疑这座建筑为何突然倒塌，以及它是否符合规划规定。

肯尼亚国家建设局在一份声明中表示，已确定了该开发项目背后的公司以及建筑师和结构工程师的身份，但没有透露周五之前是否已对现场进行了检查。

国家警察局表示已展开调查，以确定倒塌原因并确定是否有人承担刑事责任。

它在一份声明中警告说，任何被发现对疏忽或违反建筑法规负责的人都将“面临法律的全部制裁”。

内罗毕州长萨卡贾·约翰逊告诉当地媒体，该建筑的业主没有占用该建筑所需的文件。

他敦促中央政府赋予地方当局更大的权力，以惩罚“无视批准的建筑规划和安全标准的开发商”。

建筑物倒塌在内罗毕并不罕见，建筑质量差或规划不当通常被认为是造成这种情况的原因。
